**0.10.0 is a breaking release.** A meta group replaces static membership: it records every node and places every data group, so groups move between nodes and nodes join and leave a running cluster. 0.10 moves the storage and protocol format to format epoch 6. A 0.10 node refuses epoch-5 Raft WAL directories and object-storage prefixes at startup and refuses 0.9 peers, and a 0.9 node refuses 0.10 peers. The backup format stays 5, so `ursulactl restore` of 0.10 restores a 0.9 backup. There is no in-place upgrade, no rolling upgrade and no rollback.

- **If you cannot move your data yet, stay on 0.9.0.**
- **Deploy 0.10 fresh and move your data with a backup.** Install 0.10 on empty PVCs and never-used object-storage prefixes for the cold store and S3 snapshots, with the 0.9 cluster's `server.cluster_id` and `raft.group_count`. Back up 0.9 with `ursulactl backup-create` and `backup-verify` of 0.9, copy its cold objects into the 0.10 cold root, and run `ursulactl restore` of 0.10. Every restored stream answers with a new `Stream-Incarnation`.
- **`helm upgrade` from 0.9 stops at the first pod**, which finds the 0.9 data on its volume and exits. Recover with `helm rollback`. Keep the peer lists of 0.9 and 0.10 nodes apart.
- **A meta group places every data group.** Every node runs a replica of the meta group, which records every node with its lifecycle and places each data group. With more nodes than `raft.placement.replication_factor` (3 by default), a node hosts only the groups placed on it and answers `307` to a node that hosts the group.
- **Groups move and nodes join and leave a running cluster.** `ursulactl placement status`, `move`, `cancel` and `set-move-limit` move live groups between nodes. `ursulactl node cordon`, `uncordon`, `decommission`, `verify-removed`, `verify-not-removed` and `replace-disk` change a node's lifecycle. A decommission cannot be undone, and a meta voter is never decommissioned. `ursulactl` of 0.9 cannot read a 0.10 node.
- **Static membership and the rollout tooling are gone.** 0.10 refuses `raft.groups`, `raft.init_membership` and `raft.init_membership_per_group`. The membership route, the ConfigMap reservation, startup ownership, the maintenance fence and the rollout scripts are removed, and the chart updates pods only by `RollingUpdate`.
- **A node is bound to its disk.** A node on a wiped or replaced disk takes part in nothing until `ursulactl node replace-disk` releases its old root, and a superseded process fences itself. A node that cannot sync its WAL disk for `raft.wal.lease` (5 s) leads no group and answers clients `503`.
- **Elections start with a pre-vote**, so a restarted or cut-off voter leaves its groups' terms alone, and a leadership goes only to a replica that can take it. Heartbeats go out every 600 ms, and a slow link slows replication instead of stopping it.
- **Readiness reads only the node's own state.** A meta outage, or a group that lost its quorum on other nodes, no longer makes every node unready. Alert on `ursulactl wait-ready` for lost redundancy.
- **Recover the meta group first, then the data groups,** with `ursulactl recover-group --target meta` and then `--target G`. A lost quorum of disks is lost data, for the meta group as for a data group.

Known issues: [#411](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/411), [#461](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/461), [#465](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/465), [#496](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/496), [#517](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/517), [#518](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/518), [#561](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/561), [#735](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/735), [#753](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/753), [#754](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/754), and [#769](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/769) and [#862](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/862), which are new in 0.10.0. Every change is listed in the [0.10.0 release notes](https://ursula.tonbo.io/docs/release-notes#0100), and installing 0.10.0 is described in [Upgrading to 0.10](https://ursula.tonbo.io/docs/operations#upgrading-to-010).
